snapshots.title: Labs – R. C. Technical Institute
snapshots.text_content:
SECTION: Labs – R. C. Technical Institute
Engineering Graphics EG Lab located at Room no. 204, 2nd floor, Main Building. Improves spatial visualization and engineering communication. Equips students with skills essential for reading, preparing, and interpreting technical drawings. Provides hands-on practice with both manual and computer-aided drafting tools Engineering Materials Science EM Lab located at Room no. 107, 1st floor, Main Building EM lab is equipped with Metallurgical microscope with specimen, muffle furnace, disk polishing machine etc. Students learn about materials and its application in the real world. Elements of Mechanical Engineering In the Elements of Mechanical Engineering laboratory, students learn the fundamentals of mechanical systems through hands-on experiments. The laboratory contains various hand and Power tools, Charts,  models  and set ups that help in understanding theoretical concepts in a practical way. Lab is equipped with various hand and power tools, Models of Boilers, mountings, accessories, I.C. Engine, VCRS, various charts. Engineering Workshop Proficiency The Engineering Workshop Proficiency Laboratory is designed to provide students with essential hands-on skills and practical knowledge in fundamental manufacturing and fabrication processes. The primary purpose of this laboratory is to familiarize students with basic workshop tools, equipment, and techniques, enabling them to translate engineering concepts into real-world applications. The laboratory encompasses Fitting Shop , Carpentry Shop , and Plumbing Shop , where students learn through direct practice: Fitting Shop – Students are trained in measuring, marking, cutting, filing, drilling, tapping,   and assembling components with precision. This builds accuracy, patience, and attention to detail. Carpentry Shop – Students acquire skills in wood working, including measuring, cutting, planning, and joint-making. These activities develop creativity, hand–eye coordination, and an understanding of material properties. Plumbing Shop – Students learn pipe fitting, threading, cutting, and jointing techniques, along with the maintenance of plumbing systems. This fosters problem-solving abilities and practical knowledge of fluid handling systems. The  Engineering Workshop Proficiency Laboratory sessions help the students to gain the ability to convert design ideas into tangible products, preparing them for the challenges of industrial and field work in their engineering careers Mechanical Drafting MD Lab located at Room no. 204, 2nd floor, Main Building, also in computer lab Room no: 105 & GH01 Improves spatial visualization and engineering communication. Equips students with skills essential for reading, preparing, and interpreting technical drawings. Provides hands-on practice with both manual and computer-aided drafting tools (AUTO-CAD). Theory of Machines and Mechanisms The Theory of Machines and Mechanisms (TOM&M) Lab is designed to provide students with practical exposure to the principles of kinematics and dynamics of machines. The purpose of the TOM&M lab is to visualize mechanisms, which helps in grasping relative motion concepts. This lab is equipped with models of different mechanisms and equipment like ·        Working Models & Mechanisms of: Cam Analysis Apparatus. Setups to show different modes of transmissions Universal Governor apparatus Epicyclic Gear Train Apparatus. Single slider-crank. Four bar chain. Types of cams, followers, and cam/follower arrangements. Friction clutches – all types. Friction brakes – all types. Rope/belt – All types of flat and V- belts. Gear trains – all types. Measurements and Metrology The purpose of this laboratory is to familiarize students with various measuring instruments and measuring techniques. Metrology lab is equipped with various instruments like Vernier caliper, micrometer, Telescopic gauge, Height gauge, Depth gauge, Bevel protector, Sine bar, Slip gauge, Dial indicator, V block,Surface Roughness tester,  Gear tooth vernier caliper, Surface plate,etc. M & M Lab is located at Room no. 110  in the Main Building Manufacturing Engineering-I This lab enables students to conceptualize and implement small-scale projects based on computer system principles. It encourages innovation through problem identification, system design, and coding. Students gain exposure to version control, testing techniques, and structured documentation. The lab promotes teamwork, time management, and presentation skills, simulating an industry project environment. Key Equipment & Facilities: Pattern-making tools – For preparing wooden patterns with proper allowances. Moulding box, mould making tools, and split pattern – For preparing sand moulds. Demonstration of casting process – Using wax to simulate metal casting. Arc welding – To study and perform electric arc welding and analyze the effect of process parameters. Gas welding set – For oxy-acetylene welding experiments. Resistance welding machine – For spot welding operations. Soldering and brazing equipments – For metal joining operations. Forging/Smithy tools – For hot and cold forging processes, including anvil, hammers, tongs, and heating furnace. COMPUTER AIDED MACHINE DRAWING PRACTICE The purpose of this laboratory is to introduce students to the principles and applications of 2D and 3D Drawings of different machine parts in Subject of Computer Aided Machine Drawing Practice. The CAMDP lab is equipped with advanced software like AutoCAD, Solid-Works and hardware tools that enable students to design, simulate, and manufacture components with precision and efficiency. CAMDP Lab is located at Room No. 105  in the Main Building. & Room No:GH01 Guest House Building. Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Machinery The purpose of this laboratory is to familiarize students with various fluid/ flow/ Pressure measuring instruments and measuring techniques. Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic lab is equipped with various instruments like U Tube manometer, Venturimeter, Orifice meter, Rota meter, Reynolds experiment, centrifugal pump, Bernoullis experiment, Reciprocating pump, orifice etc. Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Lab is located at Room no. 512  in the Workshop II Building. THERMAL ENGINEERING-I Major Equipment: Demo models of boilers and accessories Demo models of Condenser and Cooling Tower Air compressor and heat exchanger Usage: To Demonstrate various models of boilers, accessories, condensers and cooling towers. To Demonstrate air compressor To Demonstrate Heat exchangers Importance: Connects theory with available demonstration models of boilers, accessories and cooling tower and condensers. An air compressor is a working device for demonstration. Demonstration models of heat exchangers are available which connect theory and practice at laboratory level. MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING – II The laboratory is equipped with a wide range of modern machines for practical training in manufacturing processes. It has 18 working lathe machines for operations such as turning, facing, and threading. Two horizontal milling machines are used for machining flat surfaces, slots, and gears. Four shaper machines help in producing flat and contoured surfaces. A universal drilling machine is available for drilling, reaming, and tapping operations. Precision finishing is achieved using surface grinders and cylindrical grinders. Cutting operations are performed using a hydraulic hacksaw and a flexible shaft grinder. A bench grinding machine is used for sharpening and tool grinding tasks. Students learn about the working of machines, operate various machines, and manufacture jobs as per engineering drawings. Regular maintenance is carried out to keep all machines in safe and efficient working condition. MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING -III The laboratory is equipped with a wide range of modern machines for practical training in manufacturing processes. It has 18 working lathe machines for operations such as turning, facing, and threading. Two horizontal milling machines are used for machining flat surfaces, slots, and gears. Four shaper machines help in producing flat and contoured surfaces. A universal drilling machine is available for drilling, reaming, and tapping operations. Precision finishing is achieved using surface grinders and cylindrical grinders. Cutting operations are performed using a hydraulic hacksaw and a flexible shaft grinder. A bench grinding machine is used for sharpening and tool grinding tasks. Students learn about the working of machines, operate various machines, and manufacture jobs as per engineering drawings. Regular maintenance is carried out to keep all machines in safe and efficient working condition. PLANT MAINTENANCE AND SAFETY Provides hands-on experience in maintaining and repairing industrial equipment. Enhances technical skills necessary for diagnosing and fixing machinery issues. Teaches safety protocols and proper handling of tools and equipment to prevent accidents. Demonstrates techniques to predict and prevent equipment failures, reducing downtime Tools required: set of ring spanner,fix spanner,hammer,plier,micrometer,dial guage. THERMAL ENGINEERING-II Major Equipment: 4-stroke and 2-stroke engine models Diesel engine test rig Refrigeration COP testing kit Air conditioner unit Refrigeration tools kit for maintenance and servicing Usage: Engine Models: Show working principles and cycles of IC engines. Diesel Engine Test Rig: Measure brake power, indicated power, thermal efficiency, and fuel consumption. Refrigeration COP Kit & Air Conditioner: Test cooling performance, energy use, and efficiency. Refrigeration Tools Kit: Practice fault finding, assembling, and servicing. Importance: Connects theory with hands-on practice in IC engines, refrigeration, and air-conditioning systems. TOOL ENGINEERING This laboratory caters to vital learning sessions for the final year diploma students of Mechanical Engineering, offering hands-on exposure to the concepts taught in the Tool Engineering curriculum. The laboratory is designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and industrial application, nurturing the ability to visualize, design, and understand various tooling systems with the help of demonstration models of jigs and fixtures. The primary objective of the Tool Engineering Laboratory is to provide the  students with practical insights into the design and functioning of tools used in manufacturing operations. It enables the students to: Understand the tool geometries of various cutting tools. Understand the design principles of jigs, fixtures, press tools/dies, and gauges Analyze various tool holding, locating, and clamping devices. Develop problem-solving skills through design problems and related calculations. The importance of this laboratory is to prepare the students for the industry problems in tool and die design and press tool operations. INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT The primary objective of an Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM) laboratory is to provide students with practical, hands-on experience in applying industrial engineering concepts and management techniques to real-world scenarios, enabling them to: Understand and analyze production, operations, and organizational systems. Measure, evaluate, and improve work methods, productivity, and resource utilization.( Trough method study chart preparation and work measurement techniques) Apply decision-making tools for planning, scheduling, and controlling industrial processes.(problem solving) Integrate technical and managerial skills to optimize efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness.(SQC techniques and sampling methods) In short, the IEM lab bridges theoretical learning and industrial application , preparing students to design, manage, and improve systems involving people, machines, materials, and information. IE&M  Lab is located at Room no. 103  in the Main Building CAD/CAM The CAD/CAM Laboratory is designed to provide diploma students in Mechanical Engineering with hands-on training in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) tools and technologies. It serves the following purposes: Skill Development – To equip students with the ability to design mechanical components and assemblies using industry-standard CAD software. Manufacturing Integration – To familiarize students with CAM software for generating CNC programs and simulating machining operations. Practical Application – To bridge the gap between theoretical concepts learned in classrooms and their real-world industrial applications. Industry Readiness – To prepare students for modern manufacturing environments by exposing them to digital design and automated production systems. Project Support – To assist students in executing academic projects, product prototypes, and innovation-based work under SSIP or other initiatives. Usage: Creating 2D drawings and 3D models of mechanical components. Performing product simulations, motion analysis, and stress analysis. Generating CNC codes and simulating machining processes. Understanding tool paths, cutting parameters, and production planning. Practicing with CNC simulators before operating physical CNC machines. DESIGN OF MACHINE ELEMENTS The Design of Machine Elements lab aims to familiarize students with the fundamental design principles and practical applications of various mechanical components. Through hands-on sessions and design-based tasks, students gain insights into the structural behavior, functionality, and performance criteria of commonly used machine elements. This lab bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world engineering design practices. The primary objective of this lab is to provide students with practical experience in the design and analysis of key mechanical elements, including: By working on these components, students will develop the ability to select appropriate materials, apply relevant design standards, and understand the stress and deformation behavior under different loading conditions. This lab prepares students for challenges in mechanical design and enhances their problem-solving and analytical skills in engineering design scenarios. DME  Lab is located at Room no. 206  in the Main Building POWER PLANT ENGINEERING The Power Plant Engineering (PPE) Lab is designed to help students understand the working principles, components, and performance analysis of various power generation systems such as thermal, hydro, nuclear, diesel and gas turbine power plants. Power Plant Engineering (PPE) Lab is equipped with various models of Thermal Power Plant, Nuclear (Atomic) Power Plant, Hydro Power Plant, Gas Turbine Power Plant, Lamont Boiler, Loeffler Boiler. Power Plant Engineering (PPE) Lab is located in Room no. 106 of the Main Building.

snapshots.title: Labs – R. C. Technical Institute
snapshots.text_content:
SECTION: Labs – R. C. Technical Institute
Physics Lab Equipment: Vernier calipers, screw gauge, LASER, prism, pendulum, digital gates, traveling microscope, etc. Usage: Used for conducting practical related to mechanics, optics, electricity, and modern physics. Importance: Enhances students’ conceptual understanding of physical principles through hands-on experience and precise measurement techniques. beginner-level lab focusing on foundational programming and logical thinking. Students write basic programs using languages like Python. They learn syntax, control structures, loops, arrays, and functions. Emphasis is placed on algorithm development, debugging, and structured coding practices. This lab builds confidence for advanced programming tasks. Chemistry Lab Equipment: Glassware (beakers, burettes, pipettes), electronic balance, hot plates, chemical reagents, pH meter, hot air oven, etc. Usage: Used to perform volumetric analysis, acid-base titration, water analysis, and experiments related to chemical reactions. Importance: Develops practical skills in chemical handling, analysis, and environmental awareness relevant to engineering fields. Language Lab Equipment: Computers with language learning software, headsets with microphones, internet access, projector. Usage: Used for improving listening, speaking, reading, and writing (LSRW) skills; also supports soft skill development. Importance: Helps students improve their English proficiency and workplace communication, boosting confidence for academic and professional success.

snapshots.text_content:
SECTION: Training & Placement Cell – R. C. Technical Institute
TPO Cell – Overview The Training & Placement and Industry linkage Cell of R. C. Technical Institute, Ahmedabad acts as a bridge between talented Diploma Engineering students and the industry. The Cell facilitates campus and pool campus recruitment, industrial internships, student training, industry interaction, skill development, career guidance and employability enhancement activities such as finishing school program for final year students for students across various engineering disciplines. Our objective is not only to facilitate employment, but also to prepare students for successful professional careers through continuous interaction with industry, structured training and career guidance. Industry Connect Building sustainable relationships with industries through recruitment, internships, expert sessions, visits and collaborations. Recruitment activities are coordinated with participating organizations and companies according to required their eligibility criteria, job profiles, assessment methodology and recruitment schedule. Internship & Pre-Placement Opportunities Industrial internship provides students with an opportunity to experience real workplace environments, understand industrial practices and apply their academic knowledge to practical problems. R. C. Technical Institute facilitates industry interaction and internship opportunities to support students in developing professional competencies and gaining meaningful industrial exposure. 02 Industrial internships were part of curriculum and recently as per the updated curriculum, last semester students have full time internship which prepares students as industry ready candidate in total terms.  According to that, we have different models for recruitment and internships at the cell. Model 1 – Internship + Placement / PPO 6-month internship → Performance Evaluation → Placement / PPO → Joining after Diploma Model 2 – Direct Placement Selection during the recruitment process → Joining after successful completion of Diploma Model 3 – 6-Month Internship with Stipend 6-month industrial internship → Stipend → Completion of Diploma Model 4 – 6-Month Internship without Stipend 6-month industrial internship → Practical industrial exposure → Completion of Diploma Company Registration: https://www.rcti.ac.in/tpo/placement/company/ Placement Preparation Programme The Training & Placement Cell, in collaboration with departmental TPO teams, regularly conducts a range of Placement Preparation and Career Development Programmes to enhance the employability, confidence and career readiness of Diploma Engineering students. These programmes are designed at the departmental level to address the specific career requirements of students and prepare them for successful transition from the institute to industry, higher education, government careers and entrepreneurship. Through a combination of expert sessions, interactive activities and individual guidance and career counselling, students are provided with opportunities to understand industry expectations, strengthen their professional skills and make informed career decisions. snapshots.text_content:
SECTION: About ISTE Student Chapter
The Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE) is the leading National Professional non-profit making Society for the Technical Education System in our country with the motto of Career Development of Teachers and Personality Development of Students and overall development of our Technical Education System.  Being the only national organization of educators in the field of Engineering and Technology, ISTE effectively contributes in various missions of the Union Government. The strength of ISTE is the strong base it has in technical education institutions in the country.
ISTE has an Executive Council at National level. It has active membership of more than 1,43,06 technical teachers, 5,35,000 student members, more than 3332 institutional members (including IITs, IISc., NITs and other leading technical institutions), 1488 faculty chapters and 1858 students’ chapters at National level and 19 Sections at State Level.
The major objective of the ISTE is to provide quality training programmes to teachers and administrators of technical institutions to update their knowledge and skills in their fields of activity and to assist and contribute in the production and development of top-quality professional engineers and technicians needed by the industry and other organisations.

SECTION: The major objectives of the ISTE are:
Providing quality training programmes to teachers and administrators of technical institutions to update their knowledge and skills in their fields of activity.​
To assist and contribute in the production and development of top-quality professional engineers and technicians needed by the industry and other organizations.
Providing guidance and training to students to develop better learning skills and personality.

SECTION: ISTE at R.C. TECHNICAL Institute, Ahmedabad
